**Date:** Novr 24th 1862  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1862/6
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)

Here is a note for [Mr Bourne](people/person_178.qmd) that I hope may do good service. I am not inclined to augur ill from the selling off of [Aggesden](other_books/otherbook_268.qmd), for of course tales do cease to sell after a time, and [Parker](people/person_1144.qmd) certainly has published three or four one volume ones since his [son](people/person_1143.qmd)’s death, such as [Baby Bianca](other_books/otherbook_333.qmd), [Martha Brown](other_books/otherbook_334.qmd), or [the Queen’s Maries](other_books/otherbook_335.qmd).

I am glad you will kill [Mrs Forrest](other_books/otherbook_331.qmd), only recollect to alter Victoria’s saying she would go to her. I am afraid the title would be ‘stuck at’. I should almost like to call it by some name that shewed what was the drift, such as ‘Sternness or Weakness?’ I am tired of names of places and people. I believe you are right not to put [Wishop](other_books/otherbook_257.qmd) in [your collection](other_books/otherbook_31.qmd), as you have one long autobiographical story  Somehow I cannot change from one I to another at once in the same book, but I rather think I liked Wishop the best of these two the moral about Kate’s government was so good. 

[Mr Mozley](people/person_1065.qmd) talked to me a little about [Who will go and do likewise](other_books/otherbook_265.qmd) when I was at Derby, but I do not think he perceived how much people like it. If you have another copy of a short story about a Rachel that you once offered the [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd), I think [Good Words](organizations/other_73.qmd) might be worth the risk as its pay is high

yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

**Note:** Envelope addressed to Miss Smith/ 8 Wellington Road/ Charlton/ SE postmarked Winchester 24 November 1862 and London SE 25 November 1862.
